signs.9,5: THISTLEDOWN|Market every day except when it rains, or when it is sunny.
signs.25,7: EAST CAVE|Beware of the logs. They are not just logs.
signs.21,6: MEADOW RUINS|Keep out. By order of Chancellor Vex.
signs.36,6: REEDWATER POOL|No swimming. No fishing. No asking why.

talk: pendant_ruins1
You found the Pendant of Valor! I knew you had it in you.
Two more Pendants are hidden across Varrowmere. One, they say, lies beneath Reedwater.
Find them before Vex does.
Wren! You look like you slept in a hedge.
East of here, past the cave, the old Meadow Ruins sit behind the gate.
Vex has soldiers guarding it. Cut the bushes for hearts, and mind the logs.
Fresh goods! Prices go up every time you look at them. That is just how markets work.
Energy drinks? Sold out. Some fellow bought forty and ran off to train in the woods.
They say a shrine sits at the bottom of this pool.
My grandmother swore the water drops when the old sluice upstream is shut.
Me? I just rent out the boat. Well, I would, if anyone had stolen it back for me.
Three days I have been fishing here.
So far: one boot, one cart wheel and somebody's crumpled receipt for a plushie.
Those logs in the east meadow are not logs.
I sat on one. Spent a week in hospital. The nurse said it happens more than you would think.
pendant_ruins1
Still no orders to open the north road.
I have asked for a raise twice. They gave me two more nerve and a pat on the head.
Come back with a second one of those shiny Pendants and maybe I will forget I saw you.
The north road is closed by order of the Chancellor.
Do not ask me why. I just stand here. The pay is terrible.
Two Pendants! Right, I never saw you. The road north goes up to Cinderfold.
If anyone asks, you overpowered me. Make it sound heroic.

signs.8,2: A note pinned to the shelf from Captain Brannoc:|'Back late. Don't touch my blade. And feed the pigeon.'

signs.14,11: Scratched into the rock:|"The wall to the east sounds hollow."

signs.22,16: Carved in the stone:|'The meadow's valor sleeps behind three locks.'

signs.9,4: SLUICE GATE|Property of the Chancellor's Waterworks.|Do not touch the lever. We mean it. Probably.

signs.20,24: Water stains climb to the ceiling.|Somewhere in here, the old priests could raise and lower the water at will.

signs.6,20: CINDERFOLD|Miners welcome. Soldiers tolerated. Tax collectors pushed down the well.
signs.26,6: EMBER FORGE|Property of the Chancellor. Hot. Do not lick.
signs.26,20: OVERLOOK|East, past the mountains, the towers of Ashford Castle. West, a cow. Mostly the castle.

talk: pendant_forge
Three Pendants! The Dawnblade sleeps in the old grove east of Ashford.
Take it, child, and end Vex's rule.
The forge up the mountain has burned for a hundred years. Vex's men keep it lit day and night.
They say the third Pendant, the Pendant of Embers, sits in its heart.
Mountain prices, friend. Everything costs more up here. The air is thinner and so is my patience.
I used to mine up there. Then the Gilded Hand moved in and the pay went to ten cash a day and a free hospital visit.
Mostly the hospital visit.
The Wisps in the forge? Your blade passes right through them while they blaze.
Wait until they dim, or shoot them. Fire will not hurt fire, of course.

signs.25,25: The heat is unbearable. Somewhere far above, hammers ring.

signs.4,9: DAWN GROVE|Here rests the Dawnblade, for the one who carries all three Pendants.
signs.10,8: A pen with no gate. The farmer who built it swore it was "more secure that way".

talk: Oh, another one. Sit still, this will sting.
There. Good as new. Try not to get thrown through any more windows.
Vex hides behind his magic. Nothing you swing at him will land...
...except his own spells. Strike his orbs back at him with your blade.
He may hit them back. Keep returning them.

signs.5,9: A sign, half rotted:|"HOLLOWDOWN. Population: fewer every year."

talk: I am the spirit of this river. Or what is left of it since the Chancellor started bottling it.

signs.20,6: HOLLOW QUARRY|Abandoned. The rocks are too heavy for anyone without a good glove.

talk: You are from the other side, are you not? Your colours are too bright.
Vex built this place in his own image. Two of his vaults hold what you will need: one under the black water, one in the quarry.

signs.8,9: Your own footprints lead away from the empty pedestal... but you have never been here.
signs.21,7: SHADOW KEEP|Two crystal-shaped hollows are set into the gate.

talk: I was the castle nurse, on the other side. Here I am... whatever this is.
Sit. There. All mended. He is through the east doors. End it.

signs.22,9: MARROWGATE|Biggest town this side of the Chancellor. Mind your purse.
signs.11,23: THE DIG FIELD|Thirty cash, thirty seconds. Bring your own shovel.

talk: Welcome to Marrowgate! Everything is for sale here except my opinion. That is free.
Well. It is five cash.
Fresh fish! Yesterday's fish! Fish of uncertain age!
The Chancellor's tax collectors come every Tuesday. We all go on holiday on Tuesdays.
I bake bread for the whole town. Nobody pays. They just say "put it on my tab".
I do not have a tab. I have never had a tab.
Town watch. Nothing to report. Somebody stole a plushie from a stall, but the plushie seemed happy to go.
In my day we walked to the hospital. Uphill. Both ways. After being mugged. Both ways.
Those boulders? Been there since my grandfather tried to move them. He is still trying, in a way.
Folk say a strong pair of gloves would shift them.
This is the dig field.
What will it be? We have ale, stronger ale, and a drink called "Hospital Visit".
Do not order the Hospital Visit.
Off duty. Do not tell the Captain. Especially not Brask. He takes everything personally.
I put my whole savings in the stock market. Now the stock market has my savings, and I have a lovely story.
They say a bird lives on top of Frostspire that will carry you anywhere if you play it a tune.
Do you play? No? Neither do I. I just hum at it.
tempered
That blade of yours still sings? Good. Look after it. Unlike Durn, who looks after nothing.
durn
Durn! You found him! He walked in an hour ago, covered in mud, complaining.
A deal is a deal. Give me that sword.
Brannock, smith. My brother Durn and I used to temper blades together.
He went into Whisperwood after a rare ore and never came back.
Find him, and I will make your blade sing.
Durn. Yes, the lost one. I was not lost, I was "exploring". For three months.
Keep the shoes. Bandits stole them from someone faster than me anyway.
Shh. This is a library.
The Book of Old Script is on the top shelf. Nobody can reach it. We put it there in a fit of ambition.
A good hard run into the shelf might knock it down.
Odds and Ends! Mostly ends. Have a look.
Lucky Lids! Twenty cash, pick two chests, keep what is inside.
The house always wins, but sometimes the house is having a bad day.
pendant_forge
Three Pendants? Then the old songs were true. The Dawnblade waits in the grove east of the Highlands.
Mayor Tull. I would offer you a job, but the Chancellor takes ninety percent of the town budget.
The other ten percent goes on ribbon for ribbon-cutting ceremonies. We cut a lot of ribbons.
Shooting gallery! Ten cash a round. Hit the targets, win prizes.
My husband went to buy milk three years ago. He sends letters. He is "still looking for the right milk".
I am not lazy. I am in energy-saving mode.
Clinic! Sit down, you look like you have been through a wall. Several walls.
There. All patched. No charge, the Mayor pays. Well, the Mayor promises to pay.

signs.8,22: OLD MOLE'S|Holes dug, holes filled, holes admired. Knock first.
signs.44,19: WILLOWFEN|West: the marsh. North: Whisperwood (do not go in alone). Also do not go in with friends.

talk: The marsh is full of buried things. Coins, boots, a whole cart once.
Old Mole by the west pools has a shovel. Says he is retired from digging. Has said so for forty years.

signs.11,8: BOTTLES BY BELLAMY|Empty bottles, full bottles, bottles of regret.

talk: shovel
Dig where the ground looks soft and the grass grows funny. Or just dig everywhere. Worked for me.
Old Mole. Retired. Mostly.
Want my shovel? Take it. My back says I am done, my heart says one more hole.
My back wins. It always wins.
Bellamy. Bottles. That is the whole business plan.

signs.36,6: A crude sign: KEEP OWT. THIS MEENS YOU. ALSO YOU.
signs.22,33: An overturned ore cart. Fresh scratches on the side: "DURN WOZ ERE". Tracks lead north into the trees.

talk: I am the spirit of this glade. Rest a moment.
The Tangle to the east turns travellers round. Keep heading north and the trees will let you pass.
Hah! You are no bandit. Who sent you? My brother? Brannock sent a rescuer? He never sends anything. Not even letters.

signs.14,24: NORTHREACH DOWNS|North-east: Frostspire. West: Whisperwood. South: the Highlands.

talk: Sheep? No, I keep logs. The logs keep me. It is a complicated arrangement.
Up on Frostspire there is a great bird. Old Hollis the hermit says it answers to music.
He has a kazoo. Says it is the only instrument the bird respects.

signs.23,7: HOLLIS|Hermit. Do not disturb. Unless you have soup.
signs.58,7: OLD MINE|Closed. The ore ran out. Then the miners ran out.
signs.37,8: EAGLE CRAG|A great nest sits on the peak. The bird is away. A note: BACK SOON, GONE FISHING.

got: Hollis: Here. My kazoo. Play it on Eagle Crag and the bird will come.
You got the Kazoo! Play it high on Frostspire to call the great bird.
talk: Hollis. Hermit. I came up here to get away from people, and the people keep coming up here.
The bird on Eagle Crag? It carries travellers anywhere they have been. You would need a tune to call it.
A wishing well, deep in the mine. A voice echoes up: "Throw in a hundred, I will make it worth your while."

signs.6,4: ICEMERE|The water never thaws. The fish never complain.

talk: Ice fishing! Well, lake fishing. The ice gave up years ago.
There is a cave across the water where the cold comes from. Nobody goes in. Nobody can swim that far.

got: A frost spirit breathes on you. You feel lighter.
talk: The cold is mine. Take the rod. And take this blessing: you will tire half as fast.

signs.41,8: EASTVALE|Turnips, more turnips, and on special occasions, turnips.

got: Here, take my old Bug Net. I am too old for bugs. I am into rocks now.
You got the Bug Net! Catch fairies in empty bottles.
talk: I collect bugs. And fairies, if you can catch them. Try the glade in Whisperwood.
The Chancellor taxes turnips now. So we grow them under other turnips. Hidden turnips. Tax-free.
Flour, flour everywhere. I sneeze in the shape of bread now.

signs.16,9: SOUTH: the Sunscar Desert. Bring water. Bring more water than that.

signs.10,38: THE DUKE OF SALTMARSH|He took his secrets to the grave. Also his cloak. He was very attached to it.
signs.8,37: Here lies Grimsby. He borrowed money from the wrong man. And the right man. And several others.

talk: I tend the graves. Quiet work. The residents never complain about the hours.
There is a cloak buried with the old Duke, they say. A cloak that hides you from sight.

signs.36,8: Old script is carved into the stone: [you cannot read it]

talk: Welcome to the nomad camp! We move every day. Today we moved zero metres. Tomorrow, who knows?

oldscript.36,8: The sun temple keeps its gift for those who read. Stand where the shadow of the third pillar falls at noon, and dig.

talk: A well in the tent. Do not ask. Throw in a hundred and wish.
The ruins north of here are covered in old script. My grandmother could read it. She read it to me as bedtime stories.
They were mostly about taxes.
Best beach in Varrowmere. Only beach in Varrowmere. Both true.

signs.11,8: Someone hid their winnings here. Probably from a very lucky night of cards.
A miner's stash. A note says: DO NOT TELL THE TAXMAN.
The walls are scratched with tally marks. Thousands of them.
A shadow merchant's vault. Whoever they were, they will not be needing it.
A heron has been stashing shiny things in here for years.
A bandit stash. Someone has written IOU on every coin.
Frost-cold air. Someone left a heart shard and a very sad snowman.
A smugglers' nook, smelling of salt and bad decisions.
A cool cellar under the sand. Somebody has been storing ice here. Somebody very optimistic.
